defaults.permitted_development: Across Greater London, change of use turns on the lawful existing use, the proposed use class and whether any specific permitted development route applies. rules.height_rules: There is no automatic height allowance for change of use. Any new storey, plant, flue, lift overrun or rooftop equipment is separate operational development and needs its own assessment.
rules.depth_rules: There is no fixed depth allowance. Rear additions, yards, seating areas, storage compounds or service bays are separate planning questions from the use change itself.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Greater London, the harder boundary issues are usually noise, servicing, odour, parking, deliveries, waste storage and the intensity of comings and goings near neighbouring occupiers.
rules.roof_rules: A use change does not automatically carry roof plant, vents, extraction kit or terraces with it. Those elements are assessed in their own right and can be the deciding issue for neighbours and design.
rules.materials_rules: Any external alterations such as shutters, signage, cladding, vents or changed openings should be judged as part of the wider street scene rather than as a minor afterthought to the use change.

In town, district-centre and mixed-use streets, frontage quality, servicing, odour and late-night amenity are common decision points.

restrictions.conservation_area: Conservation area status usually pushes the focus onto street presence, heritage impact and how any servicing or plant will appear in the public realm.
restrictions.listed_building: Changing the use of a listed building does not remove the need for listed building consent where internal or external works affect special character.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions can still remove an otherwise available change-of-use route in selected centres or neighbourhoods, so the exact site designation should be checked first.
